column1: # PSEUDOCODE THAT WAS TRANSCRIBED AND RUN, AND WHAT THE RUN MEASURED.
# WHAT THIS CHANNEL PROVES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.
# This skill's headline caveat is that citations are ATTRIBUTED, not verified: check.py proves
# a claim points at a real entry with a locator, never that the cited paper says what the
# document claims. Executing a pseudocode block is a THIRD thing, narrower than either:
#   check.py green     -> the citation is well-formed.
#   a row here         -> the block, transcribed literally, produces the number printed beside
#                         it. The block is self-consistent and implementable.
#   `verified:` header -> a human read the cited work. NO GAIA DOCUMENT CARRIES THIS.
# A green row here does NOT mean the algorithm is the one in the cited paper. A block can run
# perfectly and still be attributed to the wrong source -- the clipmap and Bruneton-Fresnel
# defects in source-findings.tsv were both exactly that. Do not let this file be read as
# WHY IT EXISTS. Four of the nine severe/high defects found in the 2026-09-02 review were
# invisible to reading and only appeared on execution: a NaN that scalar Python `min` hides
# and GPU `min` propagates, a droplet loop that never writes the variable it reads, a talus
# artefact whose axis was stated backwards, and a pass count wrong by 10x. Reading found none
# of them. An unrun block is an unverified block, and this file is the record of which is which.
# PROVENANCE COLUMN. `lead` = re-executed by the person recording the row, against the current tree, numbers
# below are that run's. `agent` = measured by the reviewing agent and recorded on its report,
# NOT independently re-run. The distinction is the same one the skill makes everywhere else,
# and rows are not promoted from agent to lead without an actual second run.

column2: post-process masking against domain-restricted application
column3: Gaea's claim of "no difference in results" between a mask port and a downstream Mask node -- i.e. that lerp(h, f(h), m) equals "f restricted to m"
column4: 128^2 field: default_rng(4) uniform noise, 30 box-smoothing passes, scaled to relief 17.47; binary mask over the left half; transport = a thermal-style step moving 0.15*dh to any neighbour more than 0.5 below; 'domain-restricted' freezes the exterior after every step; cells-differing threshold 1e-9. Pointwise operator (h*0.5 + 10): max difference 0.000000000, ZERO cells differing ON THIS FIELD -- the identity is algebraic and IEEE-754 rounding is not guaranteed to preserve it. Transport operator (thermal-style, moves material between cells): 1 iteration also exactly 0; then 5 iters 0.206 (1.18% of relief, 257 cells), 20 iters 0.664 (3.80%, 517 cells), 80 iters 1.162 (6.65%, 775 cells). At 80 iterations 45% of the total difference lies within 4 cells of the mask boundary, which is 6% of the domain.
column5: SOUND WITH A STATED LIMIT. The vendor's equivalence is exact for pointwise operators and for a single transport step, and diverges at the mask edge as transport accumulates. The document states it as a property of that implementation rather than a general theorem.

column2: post-process masking, mass conservation
column3: whether h + (f(h)-h)*m preserves the mass a transport operator conserves
column4: Same field and operator as the row above. The transport step conserves total mass to 1.2e-10. The post-masked result changes total mass by 17.6 units: 0.37% of all material moved at 20 iterations, 0.23% at 80, 0.22% at 200 -- it PLATEAUS as the relaxation reaches its fixed point rather than growing. A soft ramp mask does not rescue it (0.12% / 0.19% / 0.18%).
column5: DEFECT CONFIRMED and added to the document. A reviewing agent reported the same phenomenon with growth to 2.76% at 200 iterations and called it unbounded; that magnitude and that growth did NOT reproduce here, and the document states the plateau it measured rather than the report.

column2: REDUCE/EXPAND padding against the low band's volume
column3: that a Laplacian split's low band gains +27.6% (symmetric EXPAND pad) or +36.8% (edge) of the field's volume while the round-trip stays bit-exact
column4: Burt-Adelson 5-tap a=0.4, separable, L=5, 256^2, EXPAND normalised by 4. Round-trip exactness reproduces in every row (1.4e-14 to 2.3e-13 m). The MAGNITUDES DO NOT. On smoothed noise: reflect/reflect -0.15%, reflect/symmetric +0.02%, reflect/edge +2.22%, reflect/zero -15.01%, zero/reflect -9.94%. Across four surfaces the same pairs range -15.0% to +2.2% (noise), -1.0% to -11.2% (full-width ramp AND corner wedge, all negative), +0.0% to +1.1% (offset plateau). Nothing reached +27.6% or +36.8% on any field tried, and the sign is field-dependent.
column5: MECHANISM CONFIRMED, NUMBERS REJECTED. The parity argument holds -- EXPAND pads a zero-interleaved array, and only reflect preserves the even/odd lattice -- and the structural point stands: round-trip exactness is blind to low-band volume error. But the reported figures do not reproduce, and on smoothed noise 'symmetric' measured SMALLER than 'reflect', contradicting the document's own 'reflect, and only reflect'. Table replaced with the measured spread, the field-dependence stated as the finding, and the pad-mode choice re-argued from parity rather than from a measured win.

column2: support radius R(L) = 3*2^L - 2
column3: the full-res support radius of an L-level analysis-and-synthesis low band
column4: Impulse through lowfull() on 512^2, threshold 1e-15: L=1..5 gives 4, 10, 22, 46, 94 -- exactly 3*2^L - 2. Separately, sweeping the impulse over all 2^L lattice phases gives a worst case of 12, 28, 60, 124 at L=2..5, exactly 2^(L+2) - 4, about 4/3 of R(L).
column5: CONFIRMED, and EXTENDED. R(L) is the retained-phase radius; the worst case over an unaligned impulse is 2^(L+2) - 4. The document now states both and says which to size from.

column2: the halo phase rule for tiled band splitting
column3: that halo >= R(L) is insufficient and the halo must also satisfy halo = 0 (mod 2^L)
column4: L=4 (R=46, period 16), 64^2 interior tiles against a whole-domain reference. At tile origin 192 (a multiple of 16): halos 48, 64, 80, 96, 112, 128 all bit-exact 0.000000; halos 56, 60, 62 wrong by 14.55, 9.40, 5.05 m despite all exceeding R. At tile origin 193: halos 49 and 65 are bit-exact and halos 48, 64 and 80 are wrong by 2.57 m -- every one of those three is a multiple of 16 and exceeds R.
column5: CONFIRMED AS STATED, but the stated form is a special case and was generalised. The real condition is (tile_origin - halo) = 0 (mod 2^L): it is the SUB-ARRAY's origin that must land on the retained phase. 'halo = 0 (mod 2^L)' is only equivalent when tile origins are themselves multiples of 2^L. The document now carries the general rule and the origin-193 counter-example, because an offset build region silently defeats the convenient form.

column2: per-class repose: is the multi-class slippage pass order-independent?
column3: the agent first wrote that k slippage passes are order-independent 'because no pass sees another's material', then revised to the opposite before delivery -- both halves needed measuring
column4: Co-located piles on flat bedrock, 64^2, cell 1.0: sand cone (amp 12, r 8) at 32 deg under scree cone (amp 12, r 4) at 38 deg; slippage moves 0.25*excess per direction per sweep until nothing moves. Scheme A, each pass reading ONLY its own layer over bedrock: the two orders agree to 0.000e+00 m -- exactly order-independent -- and the composite surface stands at 54.58 deg. Scheme B, each pass reading the composite: composite relaxes to 38.00 deg and the two orders differ by 0.25 m. Separated (non-overlapping) piles relax to exactly 32.00 and 38.00 deg under both schemes. NOTE: my first run of this was wrong -- np.roll(t,-d) moved material UPHILL, and every pile 'relaxed' to 88 deg. Fixed to np.roll(t,d) before any number above was taken.
column5: BOTH HALVES CONFIRMED, AND THE TRADE IS REAL. Order-independence and repose-correctness are mutually exclusive here, and the agent's delivered text stated only the second. The document now carries both measurements, names the trade, and splits the recommendation: read the composite and fix the order when the deposits are geometry; read bedrock only when the stack is a splatmap, where nothing is rendered as a slope.

column2: does layered K produce caprock, cuestas AND mesas?
column3: Gaia's own prior sentence, asserted twice in the corpus, that layered erodibility produces caprock, cuestas and mesas
column4: Re-ran the agent's exp2.py unmodified (128^2, 100 m/cell, stream power + linear diffusion). Reproduced exactly as reported: contrast 4 at 4 Myr S_hard/S_soft(area) 1.597, area_hard 0.502; contrast 16 at 2 Myr S_area 1.323, area_hard 0.300, trunk relief concentration 2.29x; contrast 4 dipped 10 deg S_area 1.005 and 0.87x -- the weakest of the set, matching the outcrop-width argument.
column5: SOUND, and it CORRECTS THE SKILL. The scarp is real and measured; the mesa is not. area_hard never exceeds the 0.5 that bed thickness alone predicts and FALLS to 0.300 at 16x contrast, so the map area concentrates in the WEAK beds -- a strike valley, not a mesa top. The document states Gaia's sentence as right about cuestas and scarps and overstated about mesas, and routes the tread to the mass-wasting pass.

column2: the crater and QEM measurements as delivered by their writer
column3: Pike's transcribed coefficients, the ejecta-to-rim share, and every QEM number
column4: Re-ran w3/crater.py, w3/ejecta.py, w3/qem.py and w3/qem2.py unmodified. Pike's fits intersect at 10.5829 km (depth) and 21.2726 km (rim height) against his own stated 'about 10.6' and 'about 21.3', and 30.3524 km for rim-flank width -- the transcription round-trips. Ejecta thickness at the rim as a share of Pike rim height falls 0.967 / 0.551 / 0.265 at D = 0.05 / 0.5 / 10 km. QEM: v^T K v against analytic point-plane 2.842e-14; initial Delta 1.818e-13; Delta/(n*d^2) = 0.8830 at n = 3,4,6,8,12; over 3453 contractions mean sqrt(Delta) 0.0175 against true vertical miss 0.0031, ratio 5.60 (4.17-6.94); flat-patch boundary collapse costs exactly 0.0 even after dragging the vertex a full cell inward.
column5: ALL REPRODUCE. One note recorded rather than changed: Delta/(n*d^2) = cos^2(20 deg) is an identity of the fixture, not a discovery -- a vertical displacement against n planes each tilted 20 deg gives n*d^2*cos^2(theta) for any n. The document already says 'which is the analytic value', so it is honest as written; the load-bearing conclusion (Delta scales with valence, so sqrt(Delta) grows as sqrt(n) and is not a screen-space error) is correct and follows from the identity rather than despite it.

column2: the upslope model's zero integral and the clamp-then-renormalise rule
column3: that v.grad(h) integrates to zero over a closed terrain, so an unclamped upslope precipitation field gives half the map negative rainfall and clamping alone halves the base rate
column4: 256^2, central differences, three fields x three wind directions. Periodic domain: sum(v.grad h) = 3.6e-13 to 5.5e-12, i.e. 1.6e-19 to 8.3e-17 of sum|v.grad h| -- zero to machine precision. Non-periodic with one-sided edges: -3.4e-05 of sum|.| on smoothed noise, 5.7e-17 on an isolated Gaussian ridge. Fraction of cells with a NEGATIVE value: 50.0%, 50.1% (smoothed noise, wind 0 and 30 deg), 49.6%, 49.6% (Gaussian ridge). After clamping, mean(clamped) / mean|unclamped| = 0.50 in every one of those cases. Counter-example measured deliberately: a full-width monotonic ramp gives 0.0% negative cells and a normalised sum of exactly +1.0.
column5: CONFIRMED, and the counter-example is the useful half. The identity holds because every windward slope has a lee; a terrain with no lee (a tilted plane) does not trip it at all, which is why a tilted-plane test scene hides the bug. The document states the clamp rule, the measured 0.50x base-rate loss that makes renormalisation necessary rather than cosmetic, and the ramp counter-example.

column2: the 42 degree shoreline instability threshold, and every derived coastal number
column3: that Ashton & Murray's high-angle instability threshold is recoverable from ashton2006b's own equations, confirming the transcription of four exponents
column4: Re-ran w5/coastal.py unmodified. The zero of eq. (8)'s bracket (6/5)sin^2(psi)-cos^2(psi) and the maximum of eq. (7) BOTH give 42.3920 deg, and both equal the closed form arctan(sqrt(5/6)) = 42.3920 deg, which I recomputed independently. The paper states 'approximately 42 deg'. Table 1's breaking-angle CERC form peaks at 45.000 deg as the paper says. Unstable fraction of the 0-90 range 52.9%; W* ratio for halving A exactly 2^(3/2) = 2.8284; Bruun amplification R/S = 71.55 at h* = 8 m; Bruun retreat spanning 12.65-36.22 m (2.86x) across Cooper & Pilkey's own 4-18 m closure-depth span; A = 0.067 w^0.44 spanning only 3.74x over a 20x range of w; |mu| = 0.05389 m^2/s and the L^2 e-folding table 1.3 h / 5.4 d / 1.5 yr / 149 yr; 2^2.4 = 5.278 and 0.34/0.15 = 2.267. All reproduce.
column5: ALL REPRODUCE. Two notes. The agent's unresolved units question is resolvable and its reading is right: mu = -(1/D) dQs/dtheta with Qs in m^3/s and theta in radians gives m^2/s, so the paper's printed 'm/s2' is a typo -- the document already flags this as its own dimensional reading rather than the paper's stated units, which is the honest form and was left as written. SEPARATELY, one suggestion in the agent's report was REJECTED and not applied: it proposed back-references calling the coastal axis 'the only diffusive erosion process in the skill'. That is false -- thermal erosion is a slope-limited diffusion. The claim appears nowhere in the document itself, so nothing needed correcting; it is recorded here so it is not adopted later from the report.

column2: exact EDT and the chamfer/JFA approximations
column3: Felzenszwalb & Huttenlocher Algorithm 1's exactness, and hajdu2012's published chamfer error constants
column4: Re-ran w6/edt_error.py unmodified. FH2012 Algorithm 1 transcribed against brute force: max difference 0.000e+00 on 64^2 with 40 seeds and on a 129^2 single seed -- identical, not merely close. Chamfer max relative error on the single-centre-seed configuration: 0.0572 (3-4) and 0.0198 (5-7-11), reproducing hajdu2012's PUBLISHED constants to four decimals from an implementation that did not have them. On a rasterised polyline mask, 256^2: 3-4 max 0.05719 rms 0.03584 mean +0.00448 (systematically over-estimating); 5-7-11 max 0.01980 rms 0.01042. JFA 0.0137% of cells wrong, JFA+1 0.0076%; the doubling variant Rong & Tan reject gives 25.75% wrong. Sparse case 512^2/1000 seeds: JFA 4 px of 262144, JFA+1 exactly zero.
column5: ALL REPRODUCE. The chamfer agreement is the strongest check in the wave: an independent implementation recovering a paper's published error constants to four decimals validates both the transcription and the paper at once.

column2: a component filter is not a morphological opening
column3: that area-thresholded component removal is size-selective and shape-preserving where an opening is neither
column4: Re-ran w6/component_filter.py unmodified. 256^2 thresholded noise: 927 components, 921 under 25 px = 99.4% of components but only 6.46% of set pixels. Area filter min 25: 927 -> 6 components with 0.00% of the largest feature lost. The smallest opening that clears every sub-25-px component is r=3, and it loses 54.11% of the largest feature and shatters it into 14 pieces (r=1 loses 22.87% and still leaves 88 small components; r=2 loses 41.76% and leaves 9). Shape selectivity on a synthetic mask: the area filter keeps 40/40 px of a 1-px-wide bar and 0/16 of a compact blob; opening r=1 keeps 0/40 of the bar and 12/16 of the blob -- exactly opposite. Union-find cost 0.102 pointer hops per object pixel.
column5: ALL REPRODUCE. The shape-selectivity pair is the proof: the two operators do not merely differ in degree, they select on opposite criteria, so an opening is not a cheaper component filter.

column2: blending albedo in sRGB, and where the palette should be interpolated
column3: that sRGB-space blending is a measurable error, and the corollary about palette authoring
column4: Re-ran w6/colour_blend.py unmodified. The CIEDE2000 implementation validates against all 34 Sharma/Wu/Dalal pairs to 4.95e-05, against a table printed to 4 decimals -- so the dE00 figures rest on a checked metric. Blending in sRGB at t=0.5: dE00 up to 11.68 with luminance -36.2% (snow/forest); across t the worst is dE00 16.35 at t=0.75, luminance -48.2%; worst single channel 44.1%. Every error is negative -- the curve is concave -- and a low-contrast pair (wet rock/forest) gives dE00 0.42, which is why the bug survives review. Partition of unity: sum(w) = 0.7 and 1.3 give exactly 70.0% and 130.0% luminance, and 1.6 gives 158.3% with one channel clipped, 2.0 gives 159.9% with three -- the linear-multiplier to hue-shift transition. Height vs alpha blending: per-texel 10-90% width 0.86-0.90x depth against alpha's fixed 0.800; mixed texels at t=0.5 are 100% under alpha and 4.9-48.6% under height; composited contrast 71% of source sigma under alpha (matching 1/sqrt(2)) against 96% under height.
column5: ALL REPRODUCE, and one result cuts usefully against the naive rule. A 32-entry ramp STEPPED in linear space is 10.62x non-uniform perceptually (CoV 78.3%) against 1.79x in sRGB and 1.54x in CIELAB. So 'always work in linear' is right for compositing and wrong for authoring a palette: composite in linear, interpolate the ramp in CIELAB. The document states it that way.

column2: D8 is a spanning forest, so it cannot express braiding
column3: the document's spine -- that a single-receiver network is structurally a tree and braiding is therefore not a tuning problem
column4: Re-ran w4/d8_is_a_tree.py unmodified. 256^2 fractal dome, priority-flood filled, D8 routed: N = 65536, roots = 1020, edges = 64516, and edges == N - roots is True. Cells with more than one receiver: 0. Cycles found by traversal: 0. Undirected cycles E - N + C: 0. A graph with E = N - C and no cycles IS a forest of C trees, so the representable braid index is 1 everywhere, by construction. Same terrain under MFD: 259190 edges, 63983 cells (99.2% of the interior) with more than one receiver, 194674 undirected cycles.
column5: CONFIRMED EXACTLY, and it is a structural result rather than a measurement -- the equality E = N - roots with zero cycles is a proof on this instance, not a statistic. It is the right spine for the document because it converts 'my rivers do not braid' from a parameter complaint into a representation choice.

column2: carving a user-drawn path monotone
column3: that the downstream running minimum is O(n) and correct, and that its cost is the author's depth parameter
column4: Re-ran w4/carve_monotone.py unmodified. 512^2 terrain, 170 m relief. Path drawn ACROSS the grain: 289 of 899 segments (32.1%) run uphill; the downstream running minimum removes all of them and costs 107.89 m mean extra excavation, lowering 98.8% of samples and turning a requested 4 m channel into a 138.6 m cut. The same fix applied UPSTREAM also reaches zero uphill segments and lifts 112 samples ABOVE the original terrain -- it builds an aqueduct. Path traced ALONG a valley with +-3 cells of jitter: 4 of 71 segments (5.6%), 0.03 m mean, 4.64 m deepest.
column5: ALL REPRODUCE. The pair of failure modes is the useful part: both directions of the fix reach 'monotone' and neither reaches 'what the author asked for', and the gap between the across-grain and along-valley cases (138.6 m against 4.64 m) says the real control is where the path is drawn, not how it is repaired.

column2: does the document's own prescribed fix for the missing mesa tread actually work?
column3: its recommendation to 'run thermal after the layered hydraulic pass with a per-bed talus angle', offered as the fix for its headline negative result
column4: Synthetic butte, 192^2 at 50 m cells: a 400 m escarpment, 100 m beds, resistant talus 60 deg and weak 32 deg, relaxed to convergence. Talus limit ALONE moved the escarpment from 1.998 km to 1.996 km -- 2 m on a 2 km butte -- and area_hard went 49.61% to 48.91% against single-angle controls at 49.46% (32 deg), 49.52% (45 deg) and 49.62% (60 deg), i.e. per-bed angles are indistinguishable from one angle on that measure. Mass conserved to 1.6e-14%. Adding a weathering term on steep faces and CONTROLLING FOR TOTAL MASS REMOVED: uniform weathering destroys the landform (tread std 1.01 to 7.21 m, tread mean 500.02 to 151.01 m); bed-selective weathering gives textbook parallel retreat, scarp 1.998 to 1.360 km with the tread unchanged at std 1.01 and mean 500.02.
column5: THE PRESCRIPTION WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED. A slope limit only moves material where the slope exceeds it, so once the face sits at the limit the pass converges and nothing is undermined; retreat needs a REMOVAL term, and the per-bed quantity that matters is the weathering rate, not the talus angle. The talus angle makes the debris apron; the rate makes the landform. A SECOND defect surfaced from the same runs: area_hard cannot detect a mesa even when one is present -- it FELL to 44.66% in the run that produced correct parallel retreat, because retreat shrinks the cap and the metric counts map area. The document now measures shape (tread standard deviation, scarp position) for that question and says why the area metric is the wrong instrument for it.

column2: before / during / after -- when a user constraint meets an erosion pass
column3: the document's spine, that the timing of the constraint is the architectural choice and each arm fails differently
column4: Re-ran w7/constraint_solvers.py unmodified. Same terrain, same crest, same 200 steps. BEFORE (initial condition) keeps 18.8% of visible relief, 15 pits, skirt curvature 0.69. DURING (re-imposed every step) keeps 93.4%, 16 pits, skirt curvature 88.29 -- 128x the control. AFTER (smooth stamp) keeps 93.0%, 17 pits, curvature 1.76; the same stamp hard-edged keeps 94.1% but produces 28 pits against a control of 15. The per-step projection re-adds 4562 cell-metres on step 1 and is still re-adding 867 -- 19% of that -- on step 200, so it never reaches a fixed point. Section 4, timing each operation in isolation on 257^2: one diffusion step 516.7 us, one whole-grid projection 108.3 us (21%), bbox-restricted 25.4 us (5%).
column5: ALL REPRODUCE. The structure of the argument is what makes it worth having: DURING wins on retention and is rejected anyway, on a skirt curvature of 88.29 against 0.69 -- and section 4 exists precisely to close the obvious objection, showing the projection costs 21% of a solver step, so it is NOT rejected on cost. A recommendation that beats its rival on the rival's own strongest ground is the form this corpus should aim for.

column2: how long a drawn ridge survives hillslope diffusion
column3: the closed form A(t) = sigma/sqrt(sigma^2 + 2Dt) and the half-life n = 1.5 sigma^2/(D dt)
column4: Re-ran the same script. Predicted and measured half-life are IDENTICAL at every width tested: 30, 120, 480 and 1920 steps for sigma = 2, 4, 8, 16. Amplitude after 200 steps 0.218 / 0.408 / 0.667 / 0.873, crossing 0.5 between sigma = 4 and 8 as the crossover sigma >= sqrt(2DT/3) = 5.16 cells requires. Checked the derivation independently rather than only the arithmetic: a Gaussian under the heat equation keeps its mass while its variance grows as sigma^2 + 2Dt, so amplitude falls as sigma/sqrt(sigma^2+2Dt) and halves at t = 1.5 sigma^2/D. A ridge is a 1D profile extended along its length, so the 1D law is the right one.
column5: CONFIRMED, derivation and measurement both. Predicted == measured exactly is expected here rather than suspicious, because the closed form is exact for a Gaussian under linear diffusion -- so the run is checking the implementation, not the law. The agent reported that its first attempt used 4Dt instead of 2Dt and the measurement caught it, which is the check working as intended. The document's own caveat is correct and important: this is measured for linear diffusion ONLY and is not assumed to carry to droplet erosion or to K*A^m*S^n incision.

column2: Laplace versus biharmonic interpolation of a sparse drawn constraint
column3: that a membrane creases at the constraint and a clamped plate passes through it smoothly
column4: Re-ran the same script. 65^2, both systems assembled densely and solved exactly (residuals 2.33e-15 and 1.15e-14, so no iteration error). Height shed in the first cell off the drawn line: Laplace 4.20%, biharmonic 0.26% -- a factor of 16.5. Both are global: 92.0% and 79.9% of the domain sits above 1% of the constraint height.
column5: CONFIRMED, and one folk claim was correctly REFUSED. The textbook biharmonic overshoot did not appear -- the plate undershoot measured -2.2e-05, negligible for this configuration -- and the document says so instead of repeating the expected result. Separately the agent withdrew a claim that only Gain's (a^2-1)^2 falloff is C1 after measuring smoothstep as identical (both 0.002 m/cell against a hard cut's 40.0); the document now says what matters is THAT the weight is C1, not which one. Two folk claims tested, two corrected -- this is the behaviour the wave is meant to produce.

column2: the exact condition on lacunarity for a periodic fBm
column3: the document's own summary that the lacunarity must be 'rational with a denominator dividing the period'
column4: Re-ran w8/m1_periodic_noise.py: 6-octave fBm at period 64 wraps to 4.8e-14 at lacunarity 2.0, 3.5e-13 at 3.0 and 3.8e-14 at 1.5, and FAILS at 4.7e-02 for 1.25 and 0.51-0.58 for 1.93, 2.01 and 2.1. Then checked the stated rule symbolically with exact rationals: lacunarity p/q in lowest terms, n octaves, testing whether T*lac^k is integral for every k. The rule 'q^(n-1) divides T' predicts the outcome for 2, 3, 3/2, 5/4, 7/4, 9/8 and 5/2 at T=64 without exception, and predicts the escape -- 5/4 needs 4^5 = 1024 and does wrap at T=1024.
column5: THE MEASUREMENTS REPRODUCE AND THE DOCUMENT'S OWN SUMMARY OF THEM WAS WRONG. 5/4 has denominator 4, which divides 64, and fails anyway -- the counter-example sat two lines below the rule it disproves. Corrected in both places to q^(n-1) | T, with the reason (the highest octave is binding, because that is where the denominator has compounded most) and the escape (grow the period, do not abandon the lacunarity). SEPARATELY this corrects noise-and-warping.md, which recommends detuning lacunarity off 2: that recommendation is incompatible with a tiling build, and it costs nothing to drop there, because that document's OWN table already measures per-octave offsets recovering the pinch grid as well as the detune does (0.44 against 0.44) and a translation leaves a periodic function periodic.

column2: which padding a band split needs on a PERIODIC domain
column3: that document's recommendation of `reflect`, argued from lattice parity on an open tile
column4: Re-ran w8/m6_pyramid_padding.py. On a periodic 256^2 field, low-band step across the wrap seam as a multiple of the mean interior step, at L=5: wrap 1.19, reflect 221.53, symmetric 397.69, edge 523.04. Round trip 1.1e-16 for EVERY mode. Also the periodic phase rule: the split reproduces the infinite-periodic low band iff N = 0 (mod 2^L) -- 0.000e+00 at N=256 for L=2,3,5 and at N=252 for L=2, and wrong by up to 22% of relief at N=250.
column5: CONFIRMED, and it is an ADDITION rather than a reversal -- reflect remains right for an open tile on the parity argument this corpus measured earlier, and wrap is the only right pad when the domain wraps. The sharper point is the second one: this is the SECOND failure that surface-and-scale-space.md's own recommended validation cannot see. Its round-trip assertion is blind to a 221x seam for exactly the reason it is blind to the low band's volume error -- the error lives in how the low band and the residual divide the field, not in their sum. Both are now stated together as one blind spot with two symptoms.

column2: does a Voronoi partition reproduce the published floe-size distribution?
column3: the cheap procedural recipe -- scatter points, tessellate, call the cells floes
column4: Re-ran w9/floe_partition.py. Poisson-Voronoi fits a noncumulative slope of -0.20, -0.53 and -0.07 at N = 300, 1000, 3000 against an observed -1.79 +- 0.08; CV of cell area 0.52-0.53 against 8.8-13.1 for a true power law; the largest tenth of cells holds 0.21 of the ice against 0.88. Controls recover -1.80 and -1.99 from synthetic power laws of true -1.8 and -2.0, so the fitter is sound and the miss is the partition's. Clustered seeds, Laguerre with power-law radii, recursive fracture and Voronoi-plus-merge land between -0.76 and -1.36 across five realisations each; none arrive.
column5: NEGATIVE RESULT CONFIRMED, and the agent's own methodological correction is visible in the output and worth keeping. Its first single-seed Voronoi-plus-merge run showed -1.55 to -1.63, which looks like a near-match; the five-realisation range for that construction is -1.49 to -0.92, so a single seed can easily land there by luck. It averaged, reported -1.18, and kept the earlier number out of the document. A one-seed run of a stochastic construction is not a measurement.

column2: the sign of the chamfer distance error
column3: the document's claim that chamfer distances 'over-estimate systematically', 'everywhere', with hajdu2012's E = 0.0572 quoted as '+5.7% too far'
column4: Wrote an independent chamfer implementation (forward/backward raster scans, 3-4 and 5-7-11 masks, 201^2, single centre seed, cells beyond r = 20) and compared against the exact Euclidean distance. 3-4: most positive +0.0541 at 18.4 deg, most negative -0.0572 AT 45 DEG, 25.0% of cells reading short. 5-7-11: +0.0198 / -0.0161, 58.1% of cells reading short. Two critics reported this independently and my numbers match both to four decimals.
column5: THE DOCUMENT WAS WRONG AND ITS OWN NEXT SENTENCE DISPROVED IT. The published constant 0.0572 is the maximum UNDER-estimate, at 45 degrees, which the same paragraph derives correctly two sentences later (4/3 = 1.333 against sqrt(2) = 1.414 is SHORT by 5.7%). For 5-7-11 the majority of cells read short. The +0.45% that motivated 'systematically positive' is a MEAN over one polyline field, and the sign of a mean was attached to a magnitude that is an absolute value. Corrected to a bipolar table, and the failure row reframed from a bias to a shape: the thresholded region bulges on the diagonals and pulls in near 18 degrees.

column2: whether the printed angle expression carries the sign of mu or of -mu
column3: the document's sentence that eq. (10)'s sign 'is carried by' (6/5)sin^2(psi) - cos^2(psi)
column4: MY FIRST CHECK APPEARED TO REFUTE THE CRITIC AND WAS ITSELF WRONG. Differentiating Qs numerically with respect to psi and forming mu = -(1/D) dQs/dpsi gave the expression and mu the SAME sign at 20 and 60 degrees, which looked like a clean rebuttal. That test silently assumed the derivative is taken with respect to psi. It is not: mu is differentiated by SHORELINE ORIENTATION, and psi is the wave approach angle relative to the shore normal, which runs the other way. The physics settles it without the paper: below 42 degrees a coast SMOOTHS, which is mu > 0, and the expression measures -0.7426 at psi = 20; above it a coast roughens, mu < 0, and the expression measures +0.6500 at psi = 60.
column5: CRITIC CONFIRMED, MY REBUTTAL WITHDRAWN. The expression's ZERO is exact and verified twice (42.3920 deg by two routes); its SIGN is -mu. The document now says so in the code comment and in a warning, gives the corrected expression, and states why the error is silent and total: every regime inverts, and the threshold still lands at exactly the right angle, so the obvious check passes. Recording the failed rebuttal because the lesson generalises -- a numerical check that assumes a convention cannot test a claim about that convention.

column2: is the a-trous alternative correctly dismissed?
column3: the dismissal of an undecimated split as costing (L+1)x the field in storage against 1.33x
column4: The recommended recipe builds TWO bands, lo and hi = h - lo; (L+1)x is the cost of a full undecimated PYRAMID, which it never builds. An a-trous low band is L dilated separable convolutions in place: 2 fields, the same as the decimated version. Measured on the same kernel: support radius 46/94 px decimated against 30/62 a-trous at L = 4/5; low band under a 1/2/4/8 px shift drifts 2.23 / 4.35 / 8.02 / 12.35 m decimated and 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 a-trous; wall time 512^2 L=5 0.096 s against 0.142 s.
column5: THE DISMISSAL WAS WRONG ON ITS STATED GROUND and the alternative is the better default for the case this skill targets. For a TILED build the a-trous form needs 48% less halo at L = 5, is exactly shift-invariant where the decimated pyramid drifts metres, and makes every phase rule in the document vacuous -- for about 1.5x the arithmetic. The recommendation is now a stated crossover rather than a dismissal: decimated when untiled or when many bands are wanted (the 4^-k storage decay is what makes depth affordable there), a-trous when tiled.

column2: outcrop width, and the units the sampler actually uses
column3: w = T / sin(delta), and the resolution rule T >= 4*cellSize*sin(delta)
column4: The block builds s by adding tan(delta)*horizontal to a HEIGHT, so a bed's thickness is a VERTICAL interval of s. A vertical span T crops out over T/tan(delta); a perpendicular thickness T*cos(delta) crops out over T*cos/sin -- the same distance written two ways. Using the vertical T with T/sin overstates by 1/cos(delta): measured against the sampler's own output at 1 m cells, 0.06% at 2 deg, 1.5% at 10 deg, 15% at 30 deg and 2x at 60 deg.
column5: CONFIRMED. Invisible at the shallow dips the results table quotes and wrong at the top of the document's own stated range, which is exactly where the rule is about to be used -- the rule under-constrained, demanding 200 m at 30 deg on a 100 m grid where 231 m is needed. Formula, rule and failure row all corrected to tan, with the vertical-versus-perpendicular distinction stated. The 1.4-cells headline figure survives either way (1.42 against 1.44 cells), so no measured claim changed.

column2: does 'separated piles are unaffected either way' hold?
column3: my own earlier claim, from the per-class repose measurement
column4: Re-ran my own configuration: co-located cones give an order difference of 0.253 m under the composite scheme and 0.000 under the bedrock-only scheme, with composite slopes 38.00 and 54.58 deg -- the 0.25 m and 54.6 deg I published both reproduce exactly. But sweeping the separation of two 12 m cones at 32 and 38 deg: centres 12 cells apart still differ by 0.3803 m between orders, 16 cells by 0.0158 m, and 24 cells or more by exactly 0.0000.
column5: MY MAGNITUDE STANDS, MY QUALIFIER DID NOT. A critic reported 0.42 m for the co-located case, which did NOT reproduce -- that was a different cone configuration, and my 0.253 is what my stated setup gives. Its substantive point holds anyway: 'separated' is the wrong condition, because two piles whose peaks are apart can still have overlapping RUNOUTS, and order-independence only arrives once the runouts stop meeting. Corrected to name the runout, with the measured separation sweep.

column2: how wide is a height-blended boundary?
column3: the claim that `depth` is the transition width in weight units
column4: Re-read the measurements both critics cited from w6/colour_blend.py. There are TWO widths and the document reported one as both. Per texel the 10-90% flip takes 0.89 x depth at every depth tested (0.018, 0.089, 0.259 at depth 0.02, 0.10, 0.30). The ENSEMBLE band -- the range of t over which the surface is a visible mixture -- measures 0.56, 0.56, 0.61, essentially independent of depth and 30x wider than the per-texel figure at depth 0.02.
column5: CONFIRMED BY TWO CRITICS INDEPENDENTLY AND CORRECTED. The table was honestly labelled 'per texel'; the bolded sentence drawn from it was not, and a reader sizing a transition band from depth = 0.02 would ask for 0.018 and get 0.56. `depth` sets how DITHERED the boundary is, not how wide -- which is still the parameter worth authoring, and the table's strongest row already says why: 100% of texels mixed at t = 0.5 under alpha blending against 4.9% under height blending.

column2: is the sRGB round trip float64-exact?
column3: the claim that decode(encode(x)) over 10001 samples of [0,1] is accurate to 4.4e-16, 'i.e. float64 exact'
column4: Reproduced 4.441e-16 over 10001 samples of [0,1]. Then resampled 300001 points across [0.0030, 0.0033], where the two branches actually disagree: max round-trip error 2.325e-09, seven orders of magnitude worse.
column5: THE NUMBER IS RIGHT AND THE CONCLUSION DRAWN FROM IT WAS NOT. 4.4e-16 is a sampling artefact -- a coarse grid steps over the knot. The curve is not float64-exact; it is exact everywhere you are unlikely to sample. The practical conclusion is unchanged, because 2.3e-09 is far below 16-bit quantisation, but the document now gives the real reason rather than a lucky one.

column2: the `infinity` floor for a squared-distance transform
column3: the claim that meijster2000's `m + n` suffices as the infinity of an m x n grid
column4: Transcribed the document's own Felzenszwalb Algorithm 1 with its stated intersection formula, 64^2, single seed at (5,5), and compared against analytic Euclidean distance. INF = 1e12: max error 0.0000. INF = m+n = 128, as the document said: max error 70.7107 cells -- true 82.02 computed 11.31, because everything beyond sqrt(128) = 11.31 saturates. The correct floor must exceed m^2 + n^2 = 8192.
column5: CONFIRMED. A constant was imported across a units boundary: m+n is the infinity of Meijster's FIRST phase, which carries unsquared per-column distance, while this pass is squared throughout -- as the bullet immediately above it insists. The document's own recommended unit test, columns-then-rows == rows-then-columns, PASSES anyway because the corruption is symmetric in both orderings, so the check a reader would run is blind to it.

column2: the sign of northness against the document's own gradient convention
column3: the instruction that northness is `-sin(aspect)` because a north-up raster's row index increases southward
column4: Built a pure north-facing slope and evaluated the document's own stencil: line 73 defines H = (Z2 - Z8)/(2L) as dz/dy with +y NORTH, and line 43 defines aspect = atan2(-dzdy, -dzdx). With north low and south high, H = -1.00, dz/dx = 0, aspect = 90.0 deg, and +sin(aspect) = +1.000 -- correct for a slope that faces north. The prescribed -sin gives -1.000.
column5: CONFIRMED. `-sin` is right only if dzdy is a raw ROW difference, i.e. +y south, which is the opposite of the convention this document establishes at line 73 and uses in every curvature expression. The document switches conventions mid-file without saying so, and a reader following its own H gets exactly the inverted result its failure table exists to prevent. Corrected to state the dependency rather than a bare sign, and the failure row now names the mismatch instead of one side of it.

column1: MY OWN CORRECTIONS KEEP LANDING IN ONE COLUMN AND NOT ITS SIBLING

The sharpest: I rewrote terrain-analysis-masks.md's northness Symptom cell to say the sign DEPENDS on the dzdy convention, left the Fix cell reading `Negate the gradient; -sin(aspect)` -- one side of the very mismatch the symptom names -- and then wrote a register row claiming 'the failure row now names the mismatch instead of one side of it'. column1: bounded-dmax horizon is not recoverable from the unbounded sweep
column2: driver-fields.md, "The two fields want the same sweep"
column3: lead
column4: Flat profile, z[3]=1.0, z[40]=50.0, horizon(i)=max over j>i of (z_j-z_i)/(j-i). Unbounded answers retain only cells 40+; cell 3 is never the unbounded horizon for any i<3 and is discarded. At dmax=10 cell 3 IS the horizon for i=0,1,2 -- angles 0.3333, 0.5000, 1.0000.
column5: CONFIRMS the critic and REFUTES the document's previous claim that the two bakes are "same algorithm, same code path, two parameterisations". column1: I repeated my own recurring defect and caught it one step later
column2: hydraulic-erosion.md:14, during the olsen2004 page correction
column3: lead
column4: Bulk-replacing "olsen2004 p. 5" -> "p. 6" hit a line that was NOT the formula citation: it claimed p.5 "opens its erosion chapter". Checked the artefact after editing: the "Erosion algorithms" heading IS on p.5, so the original was right and my edit made it wrong. Reverted.
column5: Fifth instance of MY OWN CORRECTIONS LANDING BY PATTERN RATHER THAN BY CHECK. The four earlier ones were caught by reviewers; this one I caught myself, one step later, only because the same artefact was still open. The rule that works is: verify each occurrence against the source, never regex a page number across a file.
